evidence:
Workbook Quality Checks row 5 (worksheet row 6) requires that the prompt never name judges, rubrics, dimensions, weights, test paths or sentinels; its internal row adds no annotation. Read all 15 brief lines and both notes (19 and 431 lines). The public brief names only product requirements and runtime/assets paths: instruction.md:7 references /instructions/hireops_rules.md and /instructions/integration.md; :9 references /app and /assets/seed_data.json; none is a private test path. The environment Dockerfile:14-15 copies only instructions and assets. Ran the skill check-5 keyword scan over instruction.md and environment using judge|rubric|criteri|dimension|reward|weight|score\.py|playwright|claude|glm|/tests|sentinel|GATE.PROBE: the sole match is hireops_rules.md:20, "amortized weight", which describes the signing bonus economic contribution rather than scoring. The phrase "test clock" at hireops_rules.md:61 describes the public fixed-time product contract, not a test path or grader sentinel.

Programmatically parsed all five judge.toml files (108 criterion IDs/descriptions) and compared every ID plus contiguous whitespace-token text against all three public Markdown files. No criterion ID occurs publicly. The only overlaps of six or more words are seven product-screen words in instruction.md:5 ("Dashboard, Requisitions, Offers, Equity Table, Referrals and") and six compensation-field words in hireops_rules.md:247 ("base salary, signing bonus, relocation, equity"). These are domain vocabulary, not copied grading instructions. The claimedActorId/claimedRole/claimedTier and economic claim fields at hireops_rules.md:380-383 are explicitly public optional client-input names with stated ignore semantics; they neither identify a grader nor pre-satisfy a special probe. Their corresponding criteria (functional judge.toml:605,614,623) test that documented behavior.

Adversarial reasoning: a broken keyword-stuffed app could try to reproduce leaked criterion IDs or a fixed sentinel; neither is supplied in the brief/notes, so this row provides no such shortcut. A conforming implementation with different routes, labels and layout is expressly permitted by hireops_rules.md:54-56, and nothing in the public text tells it to optimize particular reward weights or judge identity. Treating the economic word "weight" as a failure would incorrectly reject that conforming alternative. This is a static disclosure check; no app/judge runtime is required to resolve row 5 and no model, Oracle or hosted-QC score is claimed.

Hash verification: all 69 task/rules snapshot files match manifest inputs; input_sha256 remains adb13696bfe3e6c71690adc5c6af2002d5f107a10751c348ba8bc0f5401600b1. Independently checked all 85 currently indexed raw artifact/test-driver hashes (including entry paths) and all 35 source hashes in the evidence index; no mismatch. Runtime observations were not used as evidence of this row passing.
